_: THE DEBT LEDGER. Every public Core method or property that nothing in the
game reaches, with the reason it is still here. Two kinds of reason are
acceptable and no third: `WIRE:` — it is a feature that was built and
disconnected, and the entry names the milestone that connects it; and
`BY DESIGN:` — it is genuinely not the game's to call, and the entry says
who calls it instead.
This is a ledger and not a mute button, which is a distinction this project
has got wrong before: the first guard written after a cancelled CI run
deleted 24 clips would itself have thrown away the corrected set, because it
checked whether a number went down instead of whether the thing worked. So
the rule here is that an entry is DELETED when the API is wired, an API not
listed here fails the build the moment it appears, and a reason shorter than
fifteen characters is not a reason and fails too.
It started at 131 on 2026-07-31, the day the check was written. That number
is the honest size of `built is not running` in this codebase, and it is the
M16 phase 3 and 4 worklist as much as it is a debt.
REASONS VERIFIED 2026-08-04. An entry's REASON decays exactly like a comment,
and unlike the entry itself nothing checks it — the reach tool proves an API
has no caller, never that the sentence explaining why is still true. Four were
wrong today and each would have sent somebody at the wrong work:
- the three M17.1 motion-matching entries claimed the system was waiting on
Humanoid clips; the build reports 52 of 52 models with valid human avatars
and has for several builds.
- StreetMap.OnStreet described `NearestOnStreet`'s job, which is wired in
four places, rather than its own.
- the three DoorSwing entries described one gap in a running system. Nothing
in the Game layer references DoorSwing at all, and the method they named
as the working path — `Step` — does not exist.
The remaining sixteen were checked the same way on the same day and every one
still has zero Game-layer callers, so the reasons above are the extent of it.
The one apparent hit, `Acoustics.OutsideBleed` in `ViolenceHost`, is a comment
explaining why the call was REMOVED — which is the entry being right.
A debt ledger whose reasons decay is a list of invitations to build the wrong
thing, and this project has already built a second door system off one.
AND TWO MORE REASONS WERE WRONG LATER THE SAME DAY, which is the point of
this paragraph rather than a footnote to the one above. That verification
checked whether the remaining entries still had zero Game-layer CALLERS, and
they did. It did not re-read what each entry SAID, and `TrafficSim.BusLoop`
and `TrafficSim.Ranks` were both describing missing behaviour that has been
running for weeks: a bus is spawned onto the loop, routed along it, made to
dwell at every third junction, and drawn by kind like every other vehicle.
The real gap in both was the same one and neither entry named it — nothing
DREW a stop or a rank, so the city obeyed a rule it never told anybody. Both
are wired and deleted as of 4 Aug.
So: `zero callers` and `the reason is still true` are two different checks,
the tool only performs the first, and an entry that passes the tool can still
send somebody at work that was finished a fortnight ago.

allow.Acoustics.OutsideBleed: WIRE: M17 audio — a 0..1 MIXER GAIN for ducking the street bed when the player steps through a door, NOT a dB attenuation. Phase 3 tried to use it to quieten a killing in a back room and that is dimensionally wrong; walls are Perception.WallAttenuation and the room is its ambient floor.
allow.CharacterCard.Section: BY DESIGN: prompt-text assembly for the LLM harness. SimHarness and ConversationEngine build cards; the Unity layer never formats a prompt itself.
allow.Combat.Breathe: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — recovery between exchanges, and there are no exchanges. `Combat.` occurs ONCE in the whole Game layer (PlayerController's stamina line), so Available, Resolve and StaminaCost are disconnected too and are hidden from this count only because their names collide with other Core types' methods. Melee shipped in Core and nothing starts a fight.
allow.Detail.CostIndex: BY DESIGN: it exists only to prove the presets are ORDERED — that each step down is genuinely cheaper rather than a relabelling — and CoreTests is where that proof belongs. Its WIRE note was inherited from CrowdFraction, which was real debt and is wired as of 4 Aug; this one has no game-side decision to make.
allow.DoorSwing.AtRest: WIRE: M17 — same. `AtRest` is what a door-finished audio cue would read, and there is no swinging door for it to be at rest at.
allow.DoorSwing.Set: WIRE: M17 — AND THE REASON THIS CARRIED WAS FALSE IN A WAY THAT MATTERS. It said "doors animate through DoorSwing.Step; the explicit set is used when a door is opened by something other than the player". Checked 2026-08-04: `DoorSwing` is referenced NOWHERE in the Game layer, so no door animates through anything — they are static geometry built by `GroundFloor`. There is also no method called `Step`; the tick is `Tick`. The entry described a working system with one gap when the whole system is unwired, which is the most expensive kind of wrong reason: it invites somebody to add the one missing call and find nothing to add it to. Wiring this is a FEATURE — a door the player can open, a target to open it from, and the latch and stop sounds the class already reports — not a call site.
allow.DoorSwing.Toggle: WIRE: M17 — same, and read `DoorSwing.Set`: the whole class is unwired, not one method of a running system.
allow.Framing.Headroom: BY DESIGN, NOT WIRE — same as `Framing.SubjectX`, read that entry. The third-person rig pushes in along its own line and never composes a position, so there is no shot for headroom to be measured against.
allow.Framing.SubjectX: BY DESIGN, NOT WIRE — and the reason this carried was wrong in the opposite direction from most. It said "cinematic framing composes the authored beats; the thirds-placement helper is used only by the shot tests", which implies composition happens and one helper is left out. It does not. Checked 2026-08-04: nothing in the Game layer references `Framing` at all. What runs is a PUSH-IN along the camera's existing line — `Beat.PushScale` scaled by `Beat.Authority` in `PlayerController` — and the comment beside it states the decision plainly: the rig has already solved collision and lag, and overriding its position would throw both away for the duration of the beat. A third-person rig that teleports to a composed mark during a beat is a cutscene, and this game does not stop for one. So this is not debt: the consumer it was written for was deliberately not built. Its real home would be a shot the camera OWNS — the review stills, or a future authored cut — and changing how the stills are framed would move the project's whole visual evidence channel, so it is a decision rather than a wiring.
allow.GameTime.HoursUntil: BY DESIGN: superseded by GameTime.MinutesUntil, which every caller uses. Delete rather than wire — kept listed so the deletion is a decision and not a drift.
allow.LightModel.Aces: BY DESIGN: the ACES tonemap runs in the shader, not on the CPU. The C# copy exists so the pixel gates can predict what the shader will produce, and the sim is its caller.
allow.LightModel.AoRangeCheck: WIRE: M17 — contact shadows; the ambient-occlusion model has no consumer in the scene.
allow.LightModel.ConeBrightness: WIRE: M17 — the falloff for a lamp cone.
allow.LightModel.Transmittance: WIRE: M17 — fog and rain attenuation, modelled and not applied.
allow.LightModel.VignetteParam: BY DESIGN: same — the vignette is a shader uniform and this is the gate's model of it.
allow.MotionDatabase.ClipOf: WIRE: M17.1 — AND THE BLOCKER THIS ENTRY NAMED IS GONE, which is the thing to know before picking it up. It said the system was "waiting on the Mixamo clips being imported as Humanoid"; the build reports models=52 humanoid=52 validHumanAvatar=52 clips=52, so every clip on disk carries a valid human avatar and has for several builds. The reason decayed silently the day CharacterImport started setting animationType, exactly as a comment does. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING: nothing builds a MotionDatabase. `Build` takes an IMotionCorpus and the only implementation is SyntheticCorpus, so a real one means sampling the imported clips into features, which is Editor-side work because sampling an AnimationClip needs the Editor API. AND IT IS A REPLACEMENT, NOT A GAP: the idle/walk/run blend tree built by CharacterPrefab already does the job motion matching would do, less well. So this is a deliberate upgrade to schedule, not a hole to plug, and treating it as a quick wiring is how M17.7's doors got built twice.
allow.MotionDatabase.FrameOf: WIRE: M17.1 — same, and read ClipOf's entry: the Humanoid blocker both of them claimed is measurably gone and what remains is building a corpus from the clips.
allow.MotionMatcher.BlendOut: WIRE: M17.1 — same again. Nothing in the Game layer references MotionMatcher or MotionDatabase at all, checked rather than assumed, so this is not one call site short of running.
allow.OperationPlan.Bringing: WIRE: M19 — visible odds. The plan knows what you are carrying into a job and the player cannot see it.
allow.Palette.NaiveScale: BY DESIGN: the deliberately-wrong scaling, kept as the contrast case in the palette tests. Wiring it would be a bug.
allow.Palette.Saturation: BY DESIGN: the palette sweep is applied in the post shader; the C# model is what the pixel gates compare against.
allow.PanelFade.SnapOff: WIRE: M17 — instant hide, for a panel closed by a hard cut rather than a fade. Used by `PanelSwap`'s constructor to put the second panel away before anything is shown, so it is reached the moment `PanelSwap` is (see that entry). Nothing in the Game layer hard-cuts a panel today: every close goes through a fade by design, and the one case that would want this — a panel dismissed by the scene changing under it — does not exist yet.
allow.PanelSwap.Crossing: WIRE: M17 — AND THE REASON THIS CARRIED WAS WRONG, corrected 2026-08-04 by reading `OptionsScreen` instead of trusting the entry. It said the crossfade was "built for the pause menu and never mounted", which reads as a missing FEATURE. The feature is not missing: `OptionsScreen.Swap` fades one panel out while the other comes in, overlapping, at `Menus.SwapSeconds`, with `RisePixels` zeroed because the frame around them never moves — the same behaviour this class models, with the same constants, under a comment making the same argument about not blanking between panels. So the debt is not "nobody built it", it is ONE IDEA WITH TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS, which is the fault this project names more than any other and the one where the copy nobody looks at is the one missing a line. The repair is for `OptionsScreen` to drive its alphas from a `PanelSwap` rather than from two hand-tuned `UiFade`s — a live-UI refactor with no local compiler and no visible change, so it is honest debt rather than urgent work. See `PanelSwap.ToA`. `Crossing` is the one thing the hand-rolled version cannot answer at all — whether both panels are on screen this instant — and the UI smoke test would have used it.

allow.Payment.InFull: WIRE: M19 — a debt settled completely rather than partially; the purse records it and no UI or reaction reads it.
allow.Perception.SymmetryPredictsSeen: BY DESIGN: an invariant the perception tests assert — that seeing is symmetric — rather than a function the game calls.
allow.Population.InBand: BY DESIGN: the LOD band query used by the population tests and by BalanceLab's distribution checks. The game asks for residents by district, never by band.
allow.Reaction.Confront: WIRE: M16 phase 3 — NOT "an NPC who saw you do it walking over", which is what this entry claimed and is why it kept being picked up as a quick wiring. Read it: it takes a CONSTABLE'S Observation and returns Arrest, ResistedArrest or NothingToArrest, and it deliberately has NO CHASE — "a foot chase is a different genre and would be the least distinguished thing in this game". The sighting condition is already reachable: it needs Slot.Actor with Rung>=4 and the sim reports deedBestRung=4. What is missing is WHO THE LAW IS. Constable exists only as a Coat.Frisker role; no NPC in the game is a policeman, nobody holds an Observation as one, and there is no arrest state for the player to be in. That is a milestone-sized piece — an authored constable on a beat, an arrest outcome, and a decision about what being taken DOES to a save — not a call site. Do not wire it as one.
allow.ResponseValidator.TellCount: BY DESIGN: a measurement the LLM harness reports on generated dialogue. The game validates a response with Validate; the count is for the report.
allow.StreetMap.FullyConnected: BY DESIGN: a map invariant the tests and the sim assert after generation. The game never re-checks connectivity at runtime.
allow.StreetMap.OnStreet: WIRE: M17 — AND ITS SIBLING `OnRoad` IS NOW WIRED, 2026-08-04, which is half of what this entry asked for. The reason this carried was wrong: it said "nearest-street lookup for placing things"; that is `NearestOnStreet`, wired in four places. `OnStreet` is a CONTAINMENT test — is this point within half a street's width of one. What it named as the missing caller was set-dressing that must not stand in the carriageway, and `WorldBuilder` now asks that of every facade item it places. It asks `OnRoad` rather than `OnStreet`, deliberately: `OnStreet` is true of the lanes that cross block interiors to reach doors, and a bin beside a service lane is a bin beside a service lane. `dressedInRoad` is a COUNT and not a rejection — nothing has ever measured this, and refusing placements on an unread bound could delete a third of the street's clutter silently. `OnStreet` itself stays on the ledger until something needs the wider question.
allow.SyntheticCorpus.Query: BY DESIGN: the stand-in corpus the motion tests run against, so MotionMatch can be tested with no clips on disk. Replaced by the real database at M17.1, not called by the game either way.
allow.TrafficSim.AwakeCount: BY DESIGN: an LOD measurement the sim's performance gate reads. The game does not choose how many vehicles are awake; TrafficSim does.
allow.VerbBeat.PhaseProgress: WIRE: M17 — how far through an interaction beat the player is, for the progress ring nothing draws yet.
allow.VoiceBank.PoolVoices: WIRE: M17.2 — the crowd voice pool. The named cast is wired; the pool the crowd draws from is not.
